_comment: The Narke anaesthesia OSCE and viva stations, as a system module shaped like a pathway so every runner (lesson, OSCE, viva, competency) works with no new code. Owns no skills; every reference is to skills/anaesthesia.json or skills/core.json. Eight stations and a viva pool over all anaesthesia skills. Station competencies are NMC CBME 2024 AS codes. Deep link id: narke-osce.
name: OSCE and viva stations
oneLine: 8 timed stations: preoperative assessment, airway, consent, airway devices, spinal and BLS

chapters.title: Approaching the patient and consent
chapters.blurb: Introduction, consent for general and for spinal anaesthesia

chapters.title: Preoperative assessment
chapters.blurb: History, drugs and fasting, ASA grade and readiness

chapters.title: Airway assessment
chapters.blurb: Mouth opening, Mallampati, thyromental distance, upper lip bite and neck movement

chapters.title: Procedures and resuscitation
chapters.blurb: Bag-mask ventilation, laryngeal mask, spinal anaesthesia and adult BLS

stations.title: Preoperative assessment and ASA grade
stations.task: A 58-year-old man with diabetes and high blood pressure is listed for an elective hernia repair tomorrow. Take a preoperative anaesthetic history, give his ASA grade, and say whether he is ready for surgery.
examinerQuestions: What ASA grade did you give, and why?
Which of his medicines would you continue on the morning of surgery, and which would you ask about?
His blood sugar is very high on the morning of surgery. What do you do?

stations.title: Airway assessment
stations.task: This patient is to have a general anaesthetic. Assess the airway and tell the examiner whether you predict difficulty with mask ventilation or laryngoscopy.
examinerQuestions: Why must the patient not say 'aah' during the Mallampati test?
Which single test is the best predictor of a difficult airway?
You predict a difficult airway. What do you do before the day of surgery?

stations.title: Consent for general anaesthesia
stations.task: A 35-year-old woman is having her gallbladder removed under general anaesthesia tomorrow. Explain the anaesthetic and take her consent.
examinerQuestions: She is worried about waking up during the operation. What do you tell her?
Which risks must always be mentioned, and why?
She asks a relative to sign for her. Is that valid?

stations.title: Consent for spinal anaesthesia
stations.task: A 45-year-old man is having a knee arthroscopy under spinal anaesthesia. He is anxious about a needle in his back. Explain the spinal and take his consent.
examinerQuestions: What will he feel during the operation?
What would you tell him about the headache after a spinal?
He takes clopidogrel. What do you do?

stations.title: Bag-mask ventilation with an oropharyngeal airway
stations.task: This manikin is an unconscious adult who is not breathing adequately but has a pulse. Open the airway, insert an oropharyngeal airway and ventilate with a bag and mask.
examinerQuestions: How fast would you ventilate a patient who has a pulse but is not breathing?
The chest is not rising. What do you do?
When would you use a nasopharyngeal airway instead?

stations.title: Laryngeal mask airway insertion
stations.task: This manikin is an anaesthetised adult weighing 70 kg for a short elective procedure. Prepare and insert a laryngeal mask airway and confirm its position.
examinerQuestions: Which size would you choose for this patient, and how did you decide?
Name a patient in whom you would not use a laryngeal mask.
There is no capnography trace after insertion. What do you do?

stations.title: Spinal anaesthesia: the procedure
stations.task: A consented adult is to have a spinal anaesthetic for a lower limb operation. Describe and demonstrate on the trainer how you would prepare for and perform the spinal, and the care in the first minutes after.
examinerQuestions: Why do you choose a space below L3 in an adult?
The patient feels an electric shock down the leg as the needle advances. What do you do?
Ten minutes after the spinal, the patient says her hands feel weak and she cannot breathe properly. What is happening and what do you do?

stations.title: Adult basic life support
stations.task: You find an adult collapsed on the ward. This manikin is the patient. Perform basic life support until the AED arrives, then use it.
examinerQuestions: How do you tell agonal breathing from normal breathing?
When do you swap the person doing compressions, and why?
What changes once a tracheal tube is in place?
